content: Lenacapavir has the potential to increase the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of nisoldipine by interfering with the hepatic and intestinal metabolism mediated by the CYP3A4 enzyme. This necessitates careful monitoring and the exercise of caution during co-administration. Lenacapavir may elevate the levels of CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months following the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. This increase could heighten the risk of adverse reactions associated with these substrates, requiring vigilant monitoring. Lenacapavir can enhance the concentration or effect of norethindrone by altering its metabolism through the CYP3A4 enzyme. Caution and monitoring are advised when these drugs are used together. Lenacapavir is known to increase the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate via its impact on CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. This interaction warrants careful observation and caution. Lenacapavir can raise the plasma levels or effects of norgestrel by affecting its metabolism through the CYP3A4 enzyme. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may further increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, potentially leading to an elevated risk of adverse effects. Monitoring is recommended. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by interfering with CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary during co-administration. Lenacapavir can elevate the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of olutasidenib by altering its metabolism via the CYP3A4 enzyme. This interaction requires careful monitoring and caution. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by affecting its metabolism through the CYP3A4 enzyme. Caution and monitoring are advised during co-administration. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by affecting its metabolism through the CYP3A4 enzyme. Caution and monitoring are advised during co-administration. This necessitates careful monitoring and caution. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by altering its metabolism through the CYP3A4 enzyme. Caution and monitoring are recommended during co-administration. Lenacapavir can elevate the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of palovarotene by interfering with its metabolism via the CYP3A4 enzyme. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If unavoidable, the palovarotene dose should be reduced by 50%.
